key_prerequisites.name: Linear Independence in Abstract Vector Spaces

sections.normalized_html:
Consider the vector space [MATH: \mathbb{R}_2[t]] of all polynomials in the variable [MATH: t] over [MATH: \mathbb R] with degrees at most [MATH: 2.]

Which of the following statements are true?

  1. [MATH: \big\{ 0,t^2 \big\}] is a linearly independent set in [MATH: \mathbb{R}_2[t]]

  2. [MATH: -5t^2] can be expressed as a linear combination of [MATH: \big\{ 0, t^2 \big\}]

  3. [MATH: \big\{ 0, t^2 \big\}] is a basis of [MATH: \mathbb{R}_2[t]]
sections.readable_text:
Consider the vector space [MATH: \mathbb{R}_2[t]] of all polynomials in the variable [MATH: t] over [MATH: \mathbb R] with degrees at most [MATH: 2.]

2. [MATH: -5t^2] can be expressed as a linear combination of [MATH: \big\{ 0, t^2 \big\}]
3. [MATH: \big\{ 0, t^2 \big\}] is a basis of [MATH: \mathbb{R}_2[t]]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false. Notice that [MATH: 1 \cdot {\color{blue}0} + 0 \cdot {\color{blue}t^2} = 0,] where the first coefficient is nonzero, so the set is linearly dependent. In general, any set that contains a zero-vector is linearly dependent.

  • Statement II is true. Indeed, [MATH: -5t^2 = 0 \cdot {\color{blue}0} + (-5) \cdot {\color{blue}t^2}.]

  • Statement III is false. Since the set is not linearly independent, it can't form a basis.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
